svg.title: RTMSF deployment architecture on GCP
svg.desc: Cloud Storage sends native FINALIZE, DELETE and ARCHIVE notifications to Pub/Sub. One active finite RTMSF worker on a private Compute Engine VM runs Routing, WOERA and PMCP through GCP adapters. Routing reads existing owned Hive tables. PMCP checks generation and bounded storage listings, then adds or drops metadata partitions through the private Dataproc Metastore Thrift endpoint. The worker renews delivery leases and acknowledges successful reconciliation; terminal input requires confirmed quarantine publication before acknowledgment. A finite fixture producer and supervisor are lab support. A separate fresh Spark JVM on the VM queries the named Hive table and reads Parquet files independently of the worker. Ordinary VM service-account credentials grant cloud access; proof files preserve retries and actual process exits. Cloud Storage and Compute Engine use current official Google Cloud product icons. Pub/Sub and Dataproc Metastore use the official Data Analytics category icon; IAM uses the official Security Identity category icon. Component labels identify these category mappings. Lab tools use plain cards.
svg.text: Private VM worker · Native catalog lifecycle and finite 24-hour serialized run verified
GCP lab project · us-east1 · rtmsf-probe-vm in us-east1-b
Lab support · one child at a time
Private VM / VPC · one active finite child
Resolve owned tables and match ordered object paths
Group partition observations within Q / T_max
Verify storage and reconcile catalog membership
Owned ADD / metadata-only DROP · bounded calls
Existing Python core · GCP adapters · ACK after reconciliation
Named Hive table SQL + Parquet rows · same VM
Worker / supervisor retries · actual exits · preserved
Observed: 12 native gates + 24 hours / 7,477 serialized cycles, with restarts. Concurrent writers and performance unmeasured.
Official icons: Storage / Compute products · Pub/Sub / Metastore: Data Analytics category · IAM: Security Identity category.
